scope: Proposition 6.3 (No splitting in the fiber class) of the manuscript “Deforming hypersymplectic four-manifolds to hyperkähler triples” (preprints/Deforming-hypersymplectic-four-manifolds-to-hyperkahler-triples-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 341 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 92c36602fb496808), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 37. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ( ˜︁ A, ˜︁ C, ˜︁ B) be any smooth closed positive triple with the same three cohomology classes as (A, C, B), and let J be the structure associated to its first two members and tamed by ˜︁ B. Then: (i) Every positive J-holomorphic curve configuration whose total class is F in Λ consists of one reduced irreducible component of class F. (ii) Through every point of X there is such a component, and distinct components of class F are disjoint. (iii) Every simple parametrization of such a component is either an embedded torus or a rational curve with total adjunction defect one. If the rational parametrization is immersed, its image has exactly one transverse positive double point and no other singularity. These statements in particular hold after any exact perturbation of the triple that preserves positivity.
